entries.why: All effectiveness conditions confirmed in the 2014 PAD conditions table. ct left empty: the Governor's approval to deduct the state's counterpart (cost-share) funds at source and pay them into the project account secures the state's own contribution to project costs, not repayment of the IDA credit or collateral for it, so 'repay' does not fit; the other conditions are administrative and match no listed type.

Financing Agreement Cr. 5345-IN Schedule 2 Section I.D (safeguard frameworks, EMPs, RAPs; Jharkhand Tribal Development Plan) and Panel report para 18 (EMPs to Bank for review and approval, not met for Bagbera and Chhotagovindpur) both confirmed.

2011 PAD covenant table confirms 'implement the Project in compliance with the Safeguard Instruments' (footnote lists the RPF and RAPs incl. Webuye-Kitale) and the KCAA restructuring covenant due 31 December 2014.

The Panel Investigation Report (2018) paraphrases the AF2 Financing Agreement and cites it exactly (18 March 2016, Schedule 2 Section I(D)(2)); text is credited as 'citing' the agreement. The Panel is a listed good source and quotes the clause specifically for this financing, so accepted, though the agreement itself was not opened.

2011 AF Project Paper para 42 (government finances resettlement and compensation; mitigation measures 'covenanted in the legal agreements') and Panel report (22 Oct 2015 suspension citing the Financing Agreement requirement on social standards) confirmed.

PAD 2011 cover (loan to THDC with Guarantee of the Republic of India) and section E covenants (RAP/EMP, entitlements before construction, monthly flow measurements, debt-to-equity not above 4 to 1) confirmed. Sovereign guarantee is repayment security, so 'repay' fits.

'none' removed: the PAD says only that there are no POLICY covenants, while listing an effectiveness condition and dated covenants, so it does not say no condition was attached. Also fixed an error: the dated covenant was a contract between EEHC and its subsidiary CEPC (Cairo Electricity Production Company), not 'the plant engineer'. Remaining terms are administrative; no listed type fits.

Project Agreement Schedule 1 eligibility criteria (autonomous bodies; business plans; self-sustaining within 10 years for PIDAs/AWBs and 7 for FOs; projected cost reduction, abiana collection and beneficiary contributions), DCA Schedule 1 para 3 (no withdrawals for new investment projects without proof of eligibility), PA Schedule 3 paras 6-7 (EIA and RAP approved before works) and Panel para 203 ('the Bank had linked the investment component to the progress of institutional reforms') all confirmed. 'fees' fits since the money depended on water-charge collection targets.

Facts confirmed in the 2004 PAD, but the PAD describes the agreements before signing ('will contain', 'will indemnify'); past-tense wording changed to 'was to'. Tags kept: the indemnity is repayment security for the guarantee; the safeguard covenants are stated for this project's IDA Project Agreements.

'law' dropped with its sentence: the sub-decree and second-tranche forestry conditions belong to the separate 2000 Structural Adjustment Credit (SDR 21.9 million, Report P-7359-KH), a different loan from the case's project credit 3365-KH; the Panel says the SAC gave leverage 'that the FCMCPP, because of its small size, did not allow', which confirms they are distinct. The project credit's own terms (DCA Schedule 4 review of management plans; Section 5.01 effectiveness) are confirmed but fit no listed type.

Loan Agreement 7045-PAN Sections 3.10 (no regularization of private titles in/adjacent to Project Protected Areas without Bank-satisfactory demarcation) and 3.11 (Parts B and C under the Resettlement Process Framework) confirmed; Parts B and C are land regularization/titling and protected areas.

DCA Cr. 2517-UNI Schedule 1 withdrawal conditions (Apapa drains/Surulere channel resettlement plans), Section 6.01(a) (draft bidding documents for contracting drain maintenance to private contractors, an effectiveness condition) and Project Agreement Section 2.01(g) (living standards at least equal) confirmed.

The Panel's Additional Review quotes Project Agreement 2.12(a) word for word and names Loan Agreement 6.01(b) as making it an effectiveness condition; it also cites PA 2.04 for the zoning deadline. Accepted as a specific, sourced citation of this loan's agreements (agreement texts returned 404). Reworded: the 1993 deadline covered 'contracting and completion', and the cited sections are now named.

Confirmed in CAO 2025 report (six of 13 affirmative covenants with no reporting obligations; Smart Campaign/GIIP covenant; Exclusion List annexed to post-2012 agreements except North Haven Thai). 'the lender' changed to 'the Cambodian lender' so a reader does not take it for IFC.

ESAP actions 1-3 (CAO para 74) and AidData 37233 security confirmed. Second sentence reworded: CAO says IFC 'sought to link' the 10th disbursement to labour fixes, then granted a one-time waiver when the client agreed the SCAP with post-disbursement dates; calling the plan 'a condition' overstated it.

CAO 2024 paras 50 and 61 confirm the general covenant on ESIA/ESMP commitments and the binding ESAP item to engage herders before construction; CAO also states IFC set no timebound conditions on herders.

CAO appraisal confirms the Line III ESAP (ESIA for Line III, separate jetty ESIA, cumulative impact assessment; ESMS expanded to Line 3 by 30 June 2024). AidData 60921 confirms 'No MIGA cover or partial risk guarantee were required' (stated as fact, untagged).

CAO appraisal confirms IFC's statement that it required Hana Indonesia to apply the PS, Exclusion List and national law; CAO saw no evidence PS application was in the Java 9&10 syndication agreement; IFC says GEA was not a contractual requirement. Kept because it is attributed as IFC's claim about its own investment terms. AidData 92603 share pledge confirmed.

Dropped 'borrowers were required to follow DEG and FMO environmental and social standards': in the ICM report this is a general statement about all DEG/FMO borrowers (bank-wide policy), not a term stated for this loan. Safeguard now rests on the ICM footnote that the 2006 Performance Standards apply because they were in force when these financing agreements were concluded, which ties the standard to this deal. 'Secured loan' is confirmed but the collateral is not described; repay kept on that basis.
No conditions_add to check (IFC advisory role only; nothing found).

2008 ESAP confirmed in CAO appraisal ('This ESAP required three actions ... within the first year'). The 2021 ESRS lists the three ESAP items but does not use 'required' for them, so 'required' changed to 'included' for 2021.

ESRS 48478 confirms the agreed ESAP items: #10 extra due diligence of the 29,600 ha already acquired; #11 PS5-aligned land acquisition procedure, RLRP if involuntary resettlement occurs, and balance-sheet provisions for compensation; €250 million loan. 'Commits' is correct for an agreed action plan written in 'will' form; the text does not claim 'required', and the ESRS calls it 'an agreed Environmental and Social Action Plan' for this financing, so it is a term of this deal rather than an intention of the company alone.

NHSFO cover of the Government of Senegal's repayment obligations confirmed on both MIGA pages. The ESRS marks the RAP and the health/safety and influx plan updates as '(ESAP item)', i.e. items in the action plan attached to the guarantee, so they are terms of this deal; reworded to say so instead of reporting them as what MIGA 'said' was being prepared. Dropped the '2022' date because the pages read show Board approval on 6 February 2023 and no ESRS date.

CAO 2025 para 2.10 confirms the lenders' ESAP 'as a condition of investment' and that revisions could not violate IFC PS, ADB SPS (2009) or EBRD PRs (2008); the only groundwater measure was review of community complaints.

Kept 'none': the CAO appraisal states the PT SMU loan got Board approval 'without any relevant ESAP items or E&S conditions of disbursement', which is a source saying no environmental and social condition was attached on this issue. Text limits the claim to the palm oil supply chain and says earlier PT Gawi loan terms were not found.
